reverse_outline.summary: Three takeaways: separate fact owners, copies need reconciliation, promises frozen once
Product page facts change at different speeds, so one update schedule misleads
Four facts need four owners; search shows reconciled copies; purchase freezes answers
Eva's jacket purchase needs content, search, price, stock and discount all correct
Each chapter opens with a Kestrel & Pine case where a fact was wrong
Roadmap of the five questions the chapters answer, in order
Product information chapter: PIM owns content and identifiers after four-system duplication
Pricing chapter: who selects prices; €179 German error fixed by start dates, comparisons
Promotions chapter: discount stacking cost €52,000 / gift cards and loyalty kept separate from discounts
Search chapter: index is a maintained copy; fix data, not engine
Inventory chapter: sellable versus physical stock; oversell fixed by owned commitments

reverse_outline.summary: Owners and sources diagnose wrong pages; start with product information chapter

results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
The outliner's eleven body summaries match p01 to p11 in the spec's order; the KEY POINTS callout matches no paragraph, as the spec intends.

results.quote: Gift-card and loyalty balances are kept apart from discounts.
results.finding: The outliner needed two summaries (discount stacking cost / gift cards kept separate). The closing sentence is not tied to the chapter's question; the spec's P2-3 gives the link (gift cards and loyalty points are balances the merchant owes, not discounts), and the draft drops it, so the sentence reads as an aside (the terms reader, item 9, says the same).
Every paragraph ties to the part claim or a supporting claim: p01-p02 state the claim, p03-p05 place and order it, p06-p10 introduce the chapters arguing P2-1 to P2-6, p11 synthesizes.

results.quote: A leftover campaign setting let two discounts combine on 2,860 Black Friday orders, costing about €52,000.
results.finding: The case is given with its cost but no sentence says what it shows (that how offers combine is a setting someone must own, or how it bears on invoices and refunds); the next sentence moves to gift cards. The other cases are each followed by what they show or what fixes them.

Boundaries p01-p02 (elaboration from Part I's rule), p02-p03 (place: 'Where we are in the order's journey'), p03-p04 ('But', contrast with 'Each must be right'), p04-p05 (sequence), p05-chapters, p06-p09 ('decides'/'treats a maintained copy') and the conclusion's summary opening express their declared relationships.

results.quote: [[inventory-and-availability]] distinguishes **physical stock from what a channel may still sell**.
results.finding: Declared: sequence, carrying over the search index that copies stock and introducing 'the last and fastest-changing fact'. The entry opens like the others, with nothing marking it as the last, fastest fact or picking up the stock figure the search index copies; both flow readers then could not see why stock follows search.

results.quote: [[commerce-search-and-discovery]] treats **the search index as a maintained copy** of product, price, stock and review data.
results.finding: Both readers call the order inside the chapter list unclear: search is a copy of stock yet precedes the inventory chapter, and the page never says why. The spec's reason (the stock figure the index shows is the question search leaves open; the part ends on the unit committed at checkout) was cut from p05 and is carried by no unit's controlling idea.

results.quote: needs a description and identifiers; search must find it, pricing must select €199, availability must confirm a unit, and the discount rules must give her €235 basket (jacket and two pairs of socks) free shipping.
results.finding: Eva's needs are listed in an order (description, search, price, availability, discount) that differs from the roadmap and chapter order that follow; both readers stopped to work out which order the part follows. p03's controlling idea fixes this order.

results.quote: But each chapter opens on a case at **Kestrel & Pine, the fictional outdoor brand** selling her jacket, where one fact was wrong.
results.finding: The brand is introduced after its jacket and customer have been used; both readers would name it first or together with Eva. The spec's flow rationale orders Eva before Kestrel & Pine (already an open question).

results.quote: But each chapter opens on a case
results.finding: Both readers found the 'But' against 'Each must be right.' a weak contrast that reads as a jump, the paragraph being one free-standing sentence.

results.draft_locus: Introduction callout; Chapters in this part ¶5
results.quote: The Black Friday oversell of 1,340 jackets shows what delayed copies cost;
results.finding: KEY POINTS cite 'the marketplace selling an empty shelf on Black Friday', but the inventory entry never mentions a marketplace (round 5 cut 'on storefronts and marketplaces'), so both readers could not be sure the two refer to the same incident.

results.quote: A leftover campaign setting let two discounts combine on 2,860 Black Friday orders, costing about €52,000.
results.finding: Two separate Black Friday incidents (discount stacking, oversell) appear in four entries with nothing distinguishing them; both readers briefly blurred them.

results.quote: Search, where shoppers find products, only shows copies, each compared with its source by a reconciliation.
results.finding: Both readers found the jump from four owners to search abrupt, with 'copies' of what left implicit and 'reconciliation' used as a known mechanism.

results.quote: Under Part I's rule of one record per fact, content, price, discount and stock need four owners, not one catalog: they change at different speeds.
results.finding: Both readers had to re-read this opening sentence: discount arrives as a fourth fact that the hook did not name (flow-A), and two reasons are bundled (flow-B). The hook names three facts, an open question at fault in the spec.

results.quote: A season typed into four systems motivates a **product information management system (PIM)**;
results.finding: Both readers found 'a season typed into four systems' cryptic and re-read it.

results.quote: start dates on prices and copy-to-source comparisons fix it.
results.finding: Both readers found the remedy too compressed: how start dates would have prevented the €179 failure is left to infer.

results.draft_locus: What the Five Answers Add Up To, and Where to Begin
results.quote: ## What the Five Answers Add Up To, and Where to Begin
results.finding: Both readers paused on 'five answers': the page framed questions (flow-A) and four facts and owners (flow-B), and the shift to five, search included, is not acknowledged. The heading is the spec's.

results.draft_locus: What the Five Answers Add Up To, and Where to Begin ¶1
results.quote: Begin with [[product-information]].
results.finding: Both readers note the close gives no reason to begin with product information beyond its being first; the spec's hand-off supplies one (the slowest fact and the identifiers every other fact is keyed on).

results.quote: The chapters ask, in order:
results.finding: flow-A only: the roadmap sentence repeats the chapter list immediately and gives no reason for the order (kept by spec decision for AC-1).

results.quote: pricing must select €199
results.finding: flow-A only: coming shortly after the KEY POINTS' '€179 German price', the reader briefly wondered which price was correct.

results.quote: the discount rules must give her €235 basket (jacket and two pairs of socks) free shipping.
results.finding: flow-A only: free shipping is counted as a discount without the page saying discounts include shipping offers.

results.quote: copy-to-source comparisons
results.finding: flow-A only: the same idea as the earlier 'reconciliation' under a new name, so the reader cannot be sure it is the same thing.

results.quote: product, price, stock and review data
results.finding: flow-A only: 'review data' appears for the first time, though reviews were never named among the catalog facts (kept by spec decision).

results.quote: Every channel shows a copy, and a copy needs a source and a reconciliation.
results.finding: 'Reconciliation' is used in KEY POINTS and in ¶2 as a known mechanism; it is explained only in Figure 2's caption.

results.quote: The €179 German price and the marketplace selling an empty shelf on Black Friday were copies nobody compared with their source.
results.finding: Both incidents are cited as known before the chapter list explains them, and 'the marketplace' is never named as the channel in the oversell entry, so the reader must connect them.

results.quote: start dates on prices and copy-to-source comparisons fix it.
results.finding: The spec asks for effective-dated prices to be glossed in a clause; 'start dates on prices' names them but nothing says how a start date would have stopped the €179 copy lingering.

results.quote: prices carry legal weight
results.finding: Asserted and never explained on the page; nothing else depends on it.

results.quote: Gift-card and loyalty balances are kept apart from discounts.
results.finding: Neither 'balances' nor the reason for keeping them apart is given; the page leaves the sentence disconnected from the double-discount case beside it.

Other terms the terms reader listed are explained in place or are named only, as does_not_know allows: 'committed (promised)' and commitments, 'stock codes and barcode identifiers' (SKU/GTIN in plain words), price selection and discount allocation to order lines (only named here per the spec), and the search index (glossed in Figure 2's caption). Part I's rule and Eva's order are in already_knows.
The introduction opens on a concrete product-page example and states a disputable claim; none of the weak patterns.
The short close synthesizes, gives a diagnostic so-what and a course of action; it adds no new idea or evidence and is not a rephrased thesis alone.
'The answers give each fact an owner and each copy a source' joins the five chapters; 'When a page is wrong, ask which fact is wrong and who owns it' gives the so-what.

results.draft_locus: What the Five Answers Add Up To, and Where to Begin ¶1
results.quote: The answers give each fact an owner and each copy a source. When a page is wrong, ask which fact is wrong and who owns it.
results.finding: The callback to the opening product page (the jacket's description, price and stock badge) is not made: round 5 cut 'on the opening page', and 'a page' now reads as any page. Neither flow reader linked the close back to the opening example.

The intro-only reader and the whole-page cold reader both give the five subjects in order: content and identifiers, price selection and channels, how discounts combine and reach invoices and refunds, the search index as a maintained copy, physical stock versus what a channel may sell.

The reader answers that the description can stay unchanged for a season while the last unit can disappear with the page open, so one schedule leaves the page right about the product and wrong about buyability, and each fact needs its own owner and path; matches expected.

The reader picks commerce-promotions for (a) via 'how offers combine and how discounts reach invoices and refunds' and commerce-search-and-discovery for (b) via the index as a maintained copy and missing synonyms; matches expected.
